## Zhongji Innolight raises $6.81B in Hong Kong's biggest listing since Alibaba, priced below maximum

A $6.81B IPO for a Chinese AI optical transceiver supplier confirms that domestic AI infrastructure capital formation continues at scale, even as U.S.-China tensions tighten the equipment supply chain. For the portfolio, this is a read on the staying power of China AI buildout demand — relevant to any name with China hyperscaler exposure.

- Chinese optical transceiver supplier Zhongji Innolight raised approximately $6.81 billion (HK$53.41 billion) in a Hong Kong IPO, pricing shares at HK$980.
- The listing is Asia's second-largest of 2026 and Hong Kong's biggest since Alibaba, though it priced below the maximum offer level.
- FactSet sentiment is neutral, consistent with the below-ceiling pricing outcome.
- The scale of the raise signals sustained capital formation appetite for Chinese AI infrastructure despite geopolitical headwinds.
